notes.text: Item C describes cutting along an open and closed subset Sigma prime of the cutting circles Sigma zero, corresponding to a subset A prime of the linked graph edges A zero. On the graph this cuts an edge at its middle and replaces it by two free edges. The marking is said to follow the operation.

The page distinguishes an operation called anodine en C when C is marked, expressed by C intersect R not equal phi and C contained in Sigma plus, from the case in which C is not marked. The two markedness conditions are carried as the author’s stated equivalence; no definition of Sigma plus is reconstructed from other pages.

The marked case is described as recoverable up to a finite ambiguity from the result of the operation. The short expression in the parenthesis and the verb remain uncertain: en près/en plus and réverser/inverser. The grammatical oddity of the first candidate is not corrected. No existence or uniqueness proof of the inverse construction is supplied on this page.

The raised C est effectivement marqué is live; its q descender crosses the cancelled line below but does not cancel the word. The low a above the Sigma-plus formula is part of the deleted il y a phrase, not a formula decoration.

The final marked clause ends with a comma before capital Mais, although both witnesses give a period. The final sentence continues beyond this page and stops here at travailler. Both handwritten folios, 14 at the head and 57 at the foot, are retained.

The original and both prepared halves were read once, including every shared witness reading. The physical row count includes inserted/cancelled rows and both handwritten folios. Sixteen first-pass evidence crops were inspected; no second reading, OCR, web consultation, or TeX compilation was performed.

The main reader excluded the first comparison item from material counts: both witnesses encode the same raised liées replacement and cancelled ordinaires, with only the serialization order changed. The handwritten phi denotes the same empty set and is a diplomatic glyph correction, not a change to the mathematical condition.
